reason: Feasibility lens. The code is easy: about 40 lines at the top of filter_output_graph that delete nodes from nodes_by_id and drop their raw_edges before OUTPUT_MOTION_RELINK. Relink's 1:1 Hungarian then re-links the survivors, and the edge filter still sees ILP alternatives. The lab can replay a pre-relink node drop from friend A's cache. The refined arm still cannot deliver, for five reasons. (1) The head cannot reach the band that holds the value. After 3 um NMS the closest raw pairs are 3.25 um apart. The public head moves peaks by a mean of 0.74 um and a max of 1.61 um, and only 10.5% of peaks move >= 1 um (exp51, 143,634 peaks). Getting a pair under 2.0 um needs >= 1.25 um of relative motion toward each other at d = 3.25 um, and 2-3 um for 4-5 um pairs, so both members would need near-maximal shifts pointing at each other. The research note puts all of the oracle value in the 4-5 um band. Restricted to <4 um, the GT-oracle collapse gives -0.0003 (44b6) / +0.0001 (6bba). So the pairs the head can merge are the ones worth about 0. (2) Direct check on test outputs (scratchpad fz_pairs.py, final graph, rounded coords): same-frame pairs under 5 um are 1,050 in exp48 and 1,051 in exp51 (head on). Pairs under 2.5 um are 32 vs 26, i.e. 0.02% of 119k nodes, below the proposal's own 0.1% KILL threshold. The head does not make duplicates converge. (3) Cost against remaining budget: it needs a V1284 capture on all 199 train videos (3-5 T4 h of ~20 left). The captured peaks must then be joined to friend A's cache node IDs, which came from a different GPU, so float TTA nondeterminism can shift integer peaks. The lab also holds edge probabilities computed at integer coordinates, while the shipped head changes them through trilinear gather. The lab can therefore test the merge but not the pipeline it would ship in. (4) There is a conflict with the division steps. Safe divisions and DaughterNet run AFTER relink, so excluding 'forks and the 2 frames after' before relink only protects ILP forks. Sisters sit 3-6 um apart right after division, and a pre-relink merge can delete a daughter that DaughterNet or safe-div would later have used. Division J is worth 0.1x, and our division TP is only 23. (5) Even if everything works, the ceiling is +0.0004/+0.0020 post-hoc, which is below LB resolution with 5 days left.
fix_if_any: Do not spend GPU on it. It can be kept as a free by-product only: if the head retrain (199-video capture) happens anyway, run one CPU count step. Count raw ILP pairs whose refined positions converge under 2.0 um, split into <4 um and 4-5 um. Proceed to the lab only if there are >= 100 GT-involved converged pairs in the 4-5 um band (expected ~0). For the lab arm, also protect every node within 6 um of a node that becomes a safe-div/DaughterNet parent's daughter candidate. Do this by running the merge after the division steps on non-fork nodes only, or by excluding pairs whose members both have a predecessor within 5 um of a common t-1 node (a sister signature). Measure it with float output coords ON in both arms.
realistic_public_gain: ~0 (+0.0000..+0.0003). Head-convergeable pairs are almost all in the <4 um band, whose oracle value is -0.0003/+0.0001. The exp51 test output shows the head leaves close-pair counts unchanged (1,050 vs 1,051). The head-free variant is measured negative (-0.002..-0.013).
